page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate average multi-core performance alongside weaker single-core capabilities. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test yielded a score of 11751.7, placing it in the middle tier, whereas the single-core CPU performance of 1107.49 is in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show significant limitations, with gzip compression scoring 19.07 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression scoring 7.38 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 10%. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression recovers to an average tier at 57.21 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth remains stable in the average range, recording 77.7 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 59.92 GB/sec for large-block write operations.

With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, which registers an average throughput of 7.81 GB/sec, and database operations, scoring 4395.88 on PassMark. It also handles Redis SET operations at 11.29 million operations per second. While small-scale LLM inference is feasible, processing larger models is constrained, as shown by the weak 8.09 tokens/sec text generation speed on a medium 7B model. The dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable performance for enterprise applications, though the lack of local storage and lower single-core speeds are key architectural tradeoffs to consider.

Equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio, though it lacks local storage and GPU hardware. Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 11751.7 and a PassMark CPU score of 13262.56. However, single-core performance is weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1107.49 and poor single-threaded compression speeds. The instance is suited for workloads such as static web serving, Redis databases, and moderate multi-threaded applications. It offers predictable resource allocation via dedicated vCPUs, making it a stable option for standard enterprise workloads that do not require high single-threaded speed or local NVMe storage.
